A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PhoniTale paper, with all 27 pages and Appendices A-D available. Text, equations, tables, images, and rendered page bodies match; differences are confined to the arXiv version/date stamp and its link.

before.justification: v1 reports original module validation, automated mnemonic evaluations, ablations, and a 51-participant recall and preference study in Sections 4-6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original validation, automated evaluation, ablation, and 51-participant human-study results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain identical transliteration, syllable segmentation, keyword matching, training losses, and verbal cue generation procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 2,870 English-Korean training pairs, 36-word evaluation set, and Korean-speaking learner population. No language, domain, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: KSS and OGR remain the comparison methods in the automated and human evaluations. The prompt and language-model comparisons in Tables 2-3 also retain identical membership.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, model settings, participant screening, and testing procedures are identical. Section 6 and Appendix D retain 51 participants, 17 per group, and three rounds of 12 words.

E4.justification: The structural-alignment, prompt, and language-model ablations are unchanged, as are the attention analyses and Appendix D.5 word-level comparisons and case studies.

E5.justification: Both retain the same standard-error reporting in Figure 3, standard deviations in Table 4, and group significance tests. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including Tables 1-4 and the appendix results. For example, Table 1 retains PHT phonetic similarity of 0.95 and perplexity of 433.41.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem definitions, loss equations, similarity function, and segmentation scoring formulation in Sections 2-3 are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about phonologically grounded mnemonic generation, performance comparable to human-authored cues, and advantages over OGR.

C2.justification: Interpretations of phonetic alignment, recall versus preference, and dictionary flexibility are unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning language coverage, short-term recall, advanced vocabulary, and missing inflected dictionary forms.

D1.justification: Architecture sizes, loss and scoring weights, data-processing tools, prompts, study materials, and resource references are identical. The updated arXiv version link does not change code or data access information.

R1.justification: Cited works and research positioning are identical, including the relationships to TransPhoner, SmartPhone, and the overgenerate-and-rank approach of Lee et al. (2024).

P1.justification: Only the first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v1 dated 7 Jul 2025 to v2 dated 27 Aug 2025. Manuscript wording, headings, authors, and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, and manuscript layout are identical throughout the main text and appendices. Rendered differences are confined to the administrative arXiv margin stamp.

improvement.justification: The main text and Appendices A-D retain identical methods, evidence, interpretations, limitations, and substantive presentation. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and its link produces no meaningful improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
